**What I did**
- Wrote `out/T1/solution.py`. It loads the 244-tensor checkpoint, drops blocks 2, 6, 10 and 14, and renumbers survivors via an old-to-new index map into a fresh dict, so rename order cannot cause collisions.
- The script fails loudly before writing if any block index 12 or higher remains, if the query_key_value weights do not form exactly the contiguous set 0..11, or if the tensor count is not 184. It also verifies every surviving block keeps all 15 tensors with identical shapes, dtypes and values.
- Ran it once. It wrote `out/T1/model.safetensors` with 184 tensors and blocks 0..11.
- Wrote `out/T1/REPORT.md` with the self-report fields: one execution, no failures, roughly two minutes.
